Definition: to walk (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively)
BiblicalUsage: hâlak is how Scripture says to walk (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively). In Exodus 2:5, the text says "and her maidens walked along by the river's side." The word keeps that same sense wherever it appears.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: hâlak tells me that obedience is not drudgery; it is trusting that God's way is the good way. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
